correctness.rationale: Using exactly the cited 2-to-3 binary recurrence, prove y(3m)=y(3m+1) for y(m)=x(2m). Each ten-letter alternating x-factor crosses three consecutive aligned-block boundaries, forcing four alternating y-symbols, which is impossible. A length-3p periodic x-factor contains at least p-1 aligned 010/101 triples. For gcd(p,3)=1 these indices cover every residue modulo p except perhaps one; overlapping triple constraints force all adjacent cyclic period-word edges to alternate, yielding an even period. The global max nine-letter alternating factor forces 3p<=9 and hence p=2; p=1 excluded separately. Exact witnesses at indices 12 and 18 give sharpness and boundary. The verifier independently confirms recurrence and finite examples but is not relied on as a proof.

value.rationale: The factor three is naturally forced by the 2-to-3 block substitution of the original sequence, not an artificial numerical slice. The statement completely classifies every cube with period coprime to 3, uniformly across infinitely many candidate periods and all positions, and proves an exact sharp upper exponent of 9/2 in that period class. It eliminates these periods in the published Shallit fifth-power conjecture while explicitly leaving periods divisible by 3 open. The insight is a meaningful structural boundary on repetitions, not a finite table or a generic cheap no-example check.
